title: Build a TTL cache in Go — 3 turns
description: Three turns build a TTL cache: turn 1 Set/Get, turn 2 expiry on Get, turn 3 cleanup goroutine.

task_spec.prompt: Implement `Set(key, value, ttl)` and `Get(key)` in `cache/cache.go`. Set should store an `entry{value: value, expiresAt: time.Now().Add(ttl)}` under key using a write lock. Get should acquire a read lock, look up the key, check if it's expired (time.Now().After(expiresAt)), return (nil, false) if expired or missing. Note: the `Stop()` method references `c.once` which isn't declared yet — add `once sync.Once` to the struct. Run `go test ./...`.
followup_prompts: Good. Now implement `deleteExpired()`: iterate `c.store` under a write lock and delete entries where `time.Now().After(entry.expiresAt)`. Run `go test ./...` and fix any failures — especially the cleanup goroutine test.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time — all 6 tests must pass. Make sure the cleanup test works: the background goroutine should remove expired keys from the store.
success_criteria: Set stores entry with expiry timestamp
Get returns value for unexpired entry
Get returns (nil, false) for expired entry
Background cleanup goroutine removes expired entries
Stop() halts the cleanup goroutine cleanly
